$comment: Inline-asm P5, CROSS-CU (D-MIR-MERGE-INLINE-ASM-CLONE-ARM-MISSING). ★★★ THE ONE THING THAT MAKES THIS EXAMPLE DIFFERENT FROM `c_inline_asm_extended` IS THE `sources` ARRAY, AND IT IS NOT A STYLE CHOICE: `mir/merge/mir_merge.hpp` states the driver rule that the byte-identical single-CU path is kept for N==1 and `mergeCuMirs` runs ONLY for N>=2, so every one-source inline-asm example in this corpus is compiled by a path with no cross-CU clone in it. The cross-CU clone shipped with NO `InlineAsm` arm from the day the opcode landed, and ✔MEASURED 2026-08-17 a 2-TU build carrying any `__asm__` ABORTED the compiler (`dss::MirBuilder fatal: addInst: opcode 'inlineasm' has a dedicated builder`) at BOTH configs, with no diagnostic and no artifact — killing four of five sqlite legs the moment `--scanstatus` pulled in `src/hwtime.h`. ⚠ DO NOT 'SIMPLIFY' THIS BACK TO A SINGLE SOURCE: collapsing `sources` to one file silently restores the exact blind spot this example was written to close, and every assertion below would still pass. ★★ THE RELEASE ARM IS MANDATORY, NOT DECORATIVE: on aarch64 the pin is a clobber list protecting eight CROSS-CU-call-derived values held live across the asm, and debug does not discriminate because locals are memory-resident before mem2reg. The x86_64 arm asserts MONOTONE-OR-EQUAL on two `rdtsc` reads — the only value-independent property a counter has — so the exit code is STRUCTURE-dependent, never value-dependent. ⚠ WHY THE COUNTER-READ ARM IS x86_64-ONLY, stated from THIS lane's own measurement rather than re-quoted: ✔MEASURED 2026-08-17 that compiling the `"=a"(lo), "=d"(hi)` shape for `arm64:elf64-aarch64-linux-exec` is refused with `error[S0065]: inline-asm operand 0 uses constraint letter 'a' (from "=a"), which target 'arm64' does not declare` — the register-PINNING constraint letters `hwtime.h` relies on are an x86 vocabulary, and `rdtsc` is an x86 instruction. So aarch64 gets the clobber pin instead, which is the property THAT architecture can witness. ⓘ The sibling example additionally records that no shipped dialect declares the `%N` operand placeholder; that claim is NOT re-measured here and nothing in this example depends on it — neither arm's template contains a `%N`.
